target: 如果你曾真心在乎我，如果你曾觉得我值得你花时间……那就与我一同留在这里，在虚无的寂静中永远安息吧。
migration_authority_source: If ever you did love me, if ever you did find me worthy of your time... then you will join me here in the quiet of oblivion, and take up an eternal rest.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: If it would purchase her one single shred of happiness, I would overlook nearly anything in the world for Gerta.
target: 但只要能为她换来哪怕一丝幸福，为了格尔塔，这世上几乎任何事我都可以不计较。
migration_authority_source: If it would purchase her one single shred of happiness, I would overlook nearly anything in the world for Gerta.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: If only Astrid was still alive, or haunted these walls as I, we could ask her.
target: 要是阿斯特丽德还活着，或者像我一样以幽灵之身徘徊在这城堡里，我们就能问问她了。
migration_authority_source: If only Astrid was still alive, or haunted these walls as I, we could ask her.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: If only I had known the kind of strength you possess when I was alive, child.
target: 孩子，要是我活着的时候就知道你拥有这样的力量，该多好。
migration_authority_source: If only I had known the kind of strength you possess when I was alive, child.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: If she could not give me an heir, she could not fulfill her duties as Queen, as she saw them. And to her, that was the gravest failing of all.
target: 在她看来，如果不能为我生下继承人，就无法履行王后的职责。而对她而言，这是最严重的失职。
migration_authority_source: If she could not give me an heir, she could not fulfill her duties as Queen, as she saw them. And to her, that was the gravest failing of all.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: If this is the future you desire, choose it with intent, Ophelia.
target: 如果这就是你想要的未来，奥菲莉娅，那就明确地选择它。
migration_authority_source: If this is the future you desire, choose it with intent, Ophelia.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: If you choose this world, go into it gladly. Do not let the inevitable pain rob the intensity of your love.
target: 如果你选择这个世界，就欣然走进去。别让不可避免的痛苦消磨你炽热的爱意。
migration_authority_source: If you choose this world, go into it gladly. Do not let the inevitable pain rob the intensity of your love.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: If you return to Elsinore again, you will again lose all memory of the fate you just chose, and you will not be able to choose it again. In other words...
target: 如果你再次回到埃尔西诺，就会再次失去关于你刚刚选择的命运的一切记忆，也无法再选择它。换句话说……
migration_authority_source: If you return to Elsinore again, you will again lose all memory of the fate you just chose, and you will not be able to choose it again. In other words...

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Impossible to tell. My mother is long dead.
target: 无从得知。我的母亲已经死去很久了。
migration_authority_source: Impossible to tell. My mother is long dead.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: In a manner of speaking. Quince is the one who kept me in that shadowy version of Elsinore. I knew Claudius was trying to murder me from the start. But...
target: 可以这么说。是昆斯把我困在了那个阴暗的埃尔西诺里。我从一开始就知道克劳狄斯想谋杀我。但是……
migration_authority_source: In a manner of speaking. Quince is the one who kept me in that shadowy version of Elsinore. I knew Claudius was trying to murder me from the start. But...

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: In another, Claudius created a conspiracy, then convinced my own men to turn against me and have me imprisoned indefinitely.
target: 在另一个世界里，克劳狄斯策划了一场阴谋，又说服我的部下反叛我，把我关了起来，永不释放。
migration_authority_source: In another, Claudius created a conspiracy, then convinced my own men to turn against me and have me imprisoned indefinitely.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: In life, I did not fight Insanity. I relinquished myself to her. I was subjugated, consumed, and finally death took me.
target: 生前，我没有与疯狂抗争。我把自己交给了她。我被她征服、吞噬，最终死亡带走了我。
migration_authority_source: In life, I did not fight Insanity. I relinquished myself to her. I was subjugated, consumed, and finally death took me.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: In plain sight of all, and accessible to those curious enough to find it.
target: 就在众人眼前，只要有足够的好奇心去寻找，就能找到。
migration_authority_source: In plain sight of all, and accessible to those curious enough to find it.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: In that case, I am at your service.
target: 既然如此，我愿为你效劳。
migration_authority_source: In that case, I am at your service.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: In that, Ophelia, is everything. You must choose, and you must then live in the world which comes from it.
target: 奥菲莉娅，这就是一切的关键。你必须做出选择，然后在由此产生的世界里生活。
migration_authority_source: In that, Ophelia, is everything. You must choose, and you must then live in the world which comes from it.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: In vague silhouettes and shadows. Memory in death is a struggle. It is faint and infrequent.
target: 只有模糊的轮廓与影子。死后回忆往事很艰难。记忆淡薄，也很少浮现。
migration_authority_source: In vague silhouettes and shadows. Memory in death is a struggle. It is faint and infrequent.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Indeed, it appears he has already done so. See for yourself if he speaks true.
target: 的确，看起来他已经这么做了。你亲自看看，他说的是否属实。
migration_authority_source: Indeed, it appears he has already done so. See for yourself if he speaks true.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Indeed. A most frightening prospect.
target: 确实。那前景实在可怕。
migration_authority_source: Indeed. A most frightening prospect.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Indeed. For a small while, the Book of Fates can make even this miracle possible.
target: 确实。《命运之书》能让这样的奇迹也成为可能，哪怕只有片刻。
migration_authority_source: Indeed. For a small while, the Book of Fates can make even this miracle possible.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Indeed. I am that body once called King Hamlet.
target: 正是。我就是那曾被称为哈姆雷特国王的躯体。
migration_authority_source: Indeed. I am that body once called King Hamlet.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Indeed. It is possible, though difficult, for me to manifest.
target: 确实。我能够显形，只是很困难。
migration_authority_source: Indeed. It is possible, though difficult, for me to manifest.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Indeed. You always knew my heart best, Gerta.
target: 的确。你一直最懂我的心，格尔塔。
migration_authority_source: Indeed. You always knew my heart best, Gerta.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Insanity—death—they have always plagued our family. My mother Astrid was no exception.
target: 疯狂——死亡——它们始终纠缠着我们的家族。我的母亲阿斯特丽德也不例外。
migration_authority_source: Insanity—death—they have always plagued our family. My mother Astrid was no exception.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Is there some unfinished buisness holding you back from making a choice?
target: 是有什么未了之事，让你迟迟无法做出选择吗？
migration_authority_source: Is there some unfinished buisness holding you back from making a choice?

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It belongs to the living. To you.
target: 它属于活着的人。属于你。
migration_authority_source: It belongs to the living. To you.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It does not.
target: 并不会。
migration_authority_source: It does not.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It felt like an instant between the last time I saw you and this awakening, now. I suppose I must have been waiting for you, then.
target: 从上次见到你，到现在这次醒来，我感觉只过了一瞬。那我想，我应该一直在等你吧。
migration_authority_source: It felt like an instant between the last time I saw you and this awakening, now. I suppose I must have been waiting for you, then.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It has lingered long past its due.
target: 它早就该消失，却一直留存至今。
migration_authority_source: It has lingered long past its due.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is Peter Quince's power that keeps me here. Ophelia has helped me realize this. We were merely the puppets to his infinite jest.
target: 是彼得·昆斯的力量把我留在这里。奥菲莉娅帮我明白了这一点。我们不过是他那无尽玩笑中的傀儡。
migration_authority_source: It is Peter Quince's power that keeps me here. Ophelia has helped me realize this. We were merely the puppets to his infinite jest.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is a sleep which one has no memory of entering.
target: 那是一场睡眠，却不记得自己何时入睡。
migration_authority_source: It is a sleep which one has no memory of entering.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is a trick invented by your own mind.
target: 这是你自己的头脑编造出来的骗局。
migration_authority_source: It is a trick invented by your own mind.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is eternally more worthwhile to fight than to give up as I did, Ophelia. Never forget that. For you, hope lingers.
target: 奥菲莉娅，抗争永远比像我这样放弃更有意义。永远别忘了这一点。你仍有希望。
migration_authority_source: It is eternally more worthwhile to fight than to give up as I did, Ophelia. Never forget that. For you, hope lingers.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is impossible, yes. It is the rules of the larger game.
target: 是的，那不可能。这是一场更大的游戏的规则。
migration_authority_source: It is impossible, yes. It is the rules of the larger game.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is like standing outside a window, watching those inside gorge themselves on a feast. I press my hands against the glass nightly.
target: 这就像站在窗外，看着里面的人在盛宴上大快朵颐。我每夜都把双手贴在玻璃上。
migration_authority_source: It is like standing outside a window, watching those inside gorge themselves on a feast. I press my hands against the glass nightly.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is not my place to pass judgement on this union. Nor is it Gertrude's, in the end.
target: 我无权评判这段结合。说到底，乔特鲁德也无权评判。
migration_authority_source: It is not my place to pass judgement on this union. Nor is it Gertrude's, in the end.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is not the sovereign Heaven we were promised, Bernardo. But it is a dreamless peace, and an untroubled one.
target: 那不是人们向我们许诺的至高天堂，贝尔纳多。但那是一份无梦、无忧的安宁。
migration_authority_source: It is not the sovereign Heaven we were promised, Bernardo. But it is a dreamless peace, and an untroubled one.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is shattered. Gone. And once you set foot back in Elsinore, you will lose all memory of what you chose.
target: 它已经破碎。消失了。而一旦你重新踏入埃尔西诺，就会失去关于自己所选命运的一切记忆。
migration_authority_source: It is shattered. Gone. And once you set foot back in Elsinore, you will lose all memory of what you chose.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is strange, how these matters bear forth.
target: 世事如此发展，真是奇妙。
migration_authority_source: It is strange, how these matters bear forth.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is tempting to flee responsibility for the lives of those you love.
target: 逃避对所爱之人生命的责任，确实很诱人。
migration_authority_source: It is tempting to flee responsibility for the lives of those you love.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is the end.
target: 结束了。
migration_authority_source: It is the end.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is the oldest, most primal power of humankind.
target: 那是人类最古老、最原始的力量。
migration_authority_source: It is the oldest, most primal power of humankind.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is with my last fragments of will that I appear to you. I do not know how long I can linger.
target: 我是凭着最后残存的意志，才得以出现在你面前。我不知道自己还能停留多久。
migration_authority_source: It is with my last fragments of will that I appear to you. I do not know how long I can linger.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It is.
target: 是的。
migration_authority_source: It is.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It matters not. My father loved her, at least in front of the court, and I remember her very little.
target: 这不重要。我的父亲爱她，至少在宫廷众人面前是如此，而我对她的记忆已经很少了。
migration_authority_source: It matters not. My father loved her, at least in front of the court, and I remember her very little.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It shall not end until Elsinore lies silent.
target: 直到埃尔西诺归于死寂，这一切才会结束。
migration_authority_source: It shall not end until Elsinore lies silent.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It will never be complete.
target: 那永远也做不完。
migration_authority_source: It will never be complete.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It's not too late to turn back!
target: 现在回头还来得及！
migration_authority_source: It's not too late to turn back!

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: It's what the dead do best.
target: 这是死者最擅长的事。
migration_authority_source: It's what the dead do best.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Leaving out the gash in your neck when they tell the tale.
target: 讲述这件事时，却不提你脖子上的那道深伤口。
migration_authority_source: Leaving out the gash in your neck when they tell the tale.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Less than one cock's crow remains.
target: 剩下的时间，已不足等到下一声鸡鸣。
migration_authority_source: Less than one cock's crow remains.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Let me give you what you came here for. We have nothing more to say to one another, after all.
target: 让我把你来这里想要的东西给你吧。毕竟，我们已经没什么可对彼此说的了。
migration_authority_source: Let me give you what you came here for. We have nothing more to say to one another, after all.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Let me give you what you desire, then. The chance to find something else. Something 'better.'
target: 那就让我给你想要的东西吧。一个寻找别的可能的机会。寻找“更好的”可能。
migration_authority_source: Let me give you what you desire, then. The chance to find something else. Something 'better.'

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Let us go away now, Ophelia. Forever.
target: 我们走吧，奥菲莉娅。永远离开。
migration_authority_source: Let us go away now, Ophelia. Forever.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Life in place of death is not always a gift. You and I know that truest of all.
target: 以生代死，并不总是恩赐。你我比任何人都明白这一点。
migration_authority_source: Life in place of death is not always a gift. You and I know that truest of all.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Merely destroying your uncle will not free me, or Ophelia.
target: 只杀死你叔叔，无法让我或奥菲莉娅得到自由。
migration_authority_source: Merely destroying your uncle will not free me, or Ophelia.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Most live life without ever experiencing such a thing. I certainly did. So shall many of these good people before us.
target: 大多数人终其一生都不曾体验过这样的幸福。我便是如此。我们面前的这些好人，许多也会如此。
migration_authority_source: Most live life without ever experiencing such a thing. I certainly did. So shall many of these good people before us.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: Most ordinary folk choose love not knowing where the future might lead.
target: 大多数普通人选择去爱时，都不知道未来会走向何方。
migration_authority_source: Most ordinary folk choose love not knowing where the future might lead.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: My brother lives.
target: 我的弟弟还活着。
migration_authority_source: My brother lives.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: My form is feeble. I feel my flesh disintegrating. I must go.
target: 我的形体很虚弱。我感觉自己的血肉正在崩解。我必须走了。
migration_authority_source: My form is feeble. I feel my flesh disintegrating. I must go.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: My memories drift away like fog. Retrieve my final writings from your father. Perhaps then we can make sense of this nothingness.
target: 我的记忆像雾一样飘散。去你父亲那里取回我最后写下的东西。也许到那时，我们就能弄明白这片虚无。
migration_authority_source: My memories drift away like fog. Retrieve my final writings from your father. Perhaps then we can make sense of this nothingness.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: My notes—my notes, taken by him, out of love, out of protection—
target: 我的笔记——我的笔记，他拿走了，出于关切，出于保护——
migration_authority_source: My notes—my notes, taken by him, out of love, out of protection—

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: My son cannot see me any longer. He seems to have no memory of ever meeting me.
target: 我儿子已经看不见我了。他似乎完全不记得自己曾见过我。
migration_authority_source: My son cannot see me any longer. He seems to have no memory of ever meeting me.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: My son, listen carefully to me.
target: 我的儿子，仔细听我说。
migration_authority_source: My son, listen carefully to me.

origins.note: 复用迁移前已审运行译文；不重新翻译正文

source: My son. Remember what I told you in life: One must prevail until no other possible method remains.
target: 我的儿子。记住我生前告诉你的话：必须坚持争取胜利，直到所有可能的办法都用尽。
migration_authority_source: My son. Remember what I told you in life: One must prevail until no other possible method remains.

source:
I remember Celeste rode in the front.

She was the head of the May parade, wearing a long white dress with a blue ribbon around her waist and flowers braided into her hair. No one had ever seen a May Queen half so pretty, they said. A trail of wagons tied together proceeded down the only street in town and there she sat at the very front, skirts trailing beneath her legs, which dangled off the wagon's edge. Her feet were bare and pale and clean, her eyes a blue to match her sash. And even I had to admit she was beautiful.

I watched her go by from just outside mum's cottage. She turned to smile at me and called out. 'Anna! Come dance with us!' She extended her hands towards me, the bells tied to her wrists tinkling faintly. We had been best friends once, after all.

But the boys who walked at her side jeered at me. 'Ugly little bitch!' one of them screeched. Another tossed a stone. 'Brown-toothed, slack-jawed, scruff-haired nothing!' One of them came after me with a stick, as though he meant to break it over my back.

Tears filling my eyes, I retreated into the woods. Far away from the raucous sounds of the May Day parade, everything here was dark and silent. The trees stretched like fingers overhead, and for a moment I forgot myself in that darkness. I knew not where I went, but walked with my eyes locked upon the mossy ground. There was no path. I needed none.

All humans know when they have truly become lost. And so I had. It was nearly midnight now, though it had been noon when I left my mother's threshold. A full moon lit my path, casting twining shadows on the forest floor. 

At last I came upon a still lake. And there I prayed to the spirit of spring herself, that great goddess whose image all May Queens were created in. 'Make me beautiful like Celeste,' I cried. 'Make me worthy of being the May Queen, too!'

The waters parted. A single wave lapped the surface. And then, slowly, the mare climbed out of the water's depths, one hoof at a time. It was a white mare, drenched through, and it shook its head wildly, flicking drops of water from its mane. Surely this must be the goddess herself, manifested in mortal form. Its mane was braided—just as Celeste's had been—but with mossweed, not flowers.

The mare stood before me, its golden eyes fixed upon me. At last it said (with no mouth that could move, but with a voice all the same) 'Child of man, have you come to seek my aid?'

'I have,' I said, quietly. 'I want to be beautiful. As beautiful as Celeste.'

It bowed its great head to me and nuzzled my hand. I touched it tenderly, its breath on my fingers. And, flooded with sudden relief that my prayer had been answered, I pressed my face into its mane and sobbed.

'Cry not, child of man,' it told me. 'Come into my dark waters and be reborn as a goddess in your own right. Merely climb on my back, and we'll descend together. You shall be a May Queen yet.'

I wrapped its mane round my fingers and pulled myself up her back with all my might, swinging one leg over her sinewy side. Together, we began to descend into the water. I felt the cold bite of it weighing down my skirts, my shoes; and before I knew it, the water was up to my chest. 

It was then I peered beneath the surface and my heart leapt into my chest. The mare was no mare, but a rotted, hulking thing, its flesh stripped in pieces from its corpse and fluttering in the water's current. The wet stink of death came upon me, and I gagged. I reached for the only thing I could grab—a branch overhanging the pond—and pulled with all my might. The creature ceased its descent beneath the water and turned upon me, its face little more than two shriveled eyes in a grinning skull.

我把它的鬃毛缠在手指上，用尽力气爬上它的背，把一条腿跨过它筋肉结实的侧腹。我们一起开始向水中下沉。我感到刺骨的冷水浸透了裙子和鞋子，坠得它们沉甸甸的；还没反应过来，水就已经漫到了胸口。 

就在那时，我往水下看去，心猛地一跳。那母马根本不是马，而是一具腐烂的庞然巨物，尸身上的皮肉一片片剥落，在水流中飘动。湿腐的死亡恶臭扑面而来，我一阵干呕。我伸手抓住唯一够得着的东西——一根伸到池塘上方的树枝——拼命往上拉。那怪物停止了下沉，转头朝向我。它的脸几乎只剩下一颗咧嘴的骷髅头，嵌着两只干瘪的眼睛。

I remember Celeste rode in the front.

She was the head of the May parade, wearing a long white dress with a blue ribbon around her waist and flowers braided into her hair. No one had ever seen a May Queen half so pretty, they said. A trail of wagons tied together proceeded down the only street in town and there she sat at the very front, skirts trailing beneath her legs, which dangled off the wagon's edge. Her feet were bare and pale and clean, her eyes a blue to match her sash. And even I had to admit she was beautiful.

I watched her go by from just outside mum's cottage. She turned to smile at me and called out. 'Anna! Come dance with us!' She extended her hands towards me, the bells tied to her wrists tinkling faintly. We had been best friends once, after all.

But the boys who walked at her side jeered at me. 'Ugly little bitch!' one of them screeched. Another tossed a stone. 'Brown-toothed, slack-jawed, scruff-haired nothing!' One of them came after me with a stick, as though he meant to break it over my back.

Tears filling my eyes, I retreated into the woods. Far away from the raucous sounds of the May Day parade, everything here was dark and silent. The trees stretched like fingers overhead, and for a moment I forgot myself in that darkness. I knew not where I went, but walked with my eyes locked upon the mossy ground. There was no path. I needed none.

All humans know when they have truly become lost. And so I had. It was nearly midnight now, though it had been noon when I left my mother's threshold. A full moon lit my path, casting twining shadows on the forest floor. 

At last I came upon a still lake. And there I prayed to the spirit of spring herself, that great goddess whose image all May Queens were created in. 'Make me beautiful like Celeste,' I cried. 'Make me worthy of being the May Queen, too!'

The waters parted. A single wave lapped the surface. And then, slowly, the mare climbed out of the water's depths, one hoof at a time. It was a white mare, drenched through, and it shook its head wildly, flicking drops of water from its mane. Surely this must be the goddess herself, manifested in mortal form. Its mane was braided—just as Celeste's had been—but with mossweed, not flowers.

The mare stood before me, its golden eyes fixed upon me. At last it said (with no mouth that could move, but with a voice all the same) 'Child of man, have you come to seek my aid?'

'I have,' I said, quietly. 'I want to be beautiful. As beautiful as Celeste.'

It bowed its great head to me and nuzzled my hand. I touched it tenderly, its breath on my fingers. And, flooded with sudden relief that my prayer had been answered, I pressed my face into its mane and sobbed.

'Cry not, child of man,' it told me. 'Come into my dark waters and be reborn as a goddess in your own right. Merely climb on my back, and we'll descend together. You shall be a May Queen yet.'

I wrapped its mane round my fingers and pulled myself up her back with all my might, swinging one leg over her sinewy side. Together, we began to descend into the water. I felt the cold bite of it weighing down my skirts, my shoes; and before I knew it, the water was up to my chest. 

It was then I peered beneath the surface and my heart leapt into my chest. The mare was no mare, but a rotted, hulking thing, its flesh stripped in pieces from its corpse and fluttering in the water's current. The wet stink of death came upon me, and I gagged. I reached for the only thing I could grab—a branch overhanging the pond—and pulled with all my might. The creature ceased its descent beneath the water and turned upon me, its face little more than two shriveled eyes in a grinning skull.

A name rose to my lips, a choked scream. 'Brook horse!'

'Yesssss,' the thing in the water hissed. Its horselike lips pulled back, revealing sharpened teeth.

I turned to swim, but felt those teeth closing down upon my back. The moon grew small, high above the surface, fading from reach. The soft green of it all surrounded me. I sank down to the moss at the bottom. No. Not moss. Remains. And the last thing I saw was that sharp, grinning smile.

'You shall never be Queen,' it rasped. 'But your bones shall be beautiful indeed.'
